h: Moshe’s Prayers Teach the Consolation of Longing

p: to the beginning of Torah she'b'al peh
which is the rebuke of Yeshayahu,
"And my heart has seen much wisdom."
For the whole matter of rebuke
הוּא כְּאָב אֶת בֵּן יִרְצֶה (מִשְׁלֵי ג, יב)
is "as a father the son in whom he delights" (Mishlei 3:12),
וְכַאֲשֶׁר יְיַסֵּר אִישׁ אֶת בְּנוֹ (דְּבָרִים ח, ה)
and "as a man chastens his son" (Devarim 8:5);
בְּלִבּוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם וְכוּלֵּי (בְּרָכוֹת ז, א)
in a person's heart is better," etc. (Berachos 7a).
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר שָׁם (יְשַׁעְיָה א, יח)
And about this it says there (Yeshayahu 1:18):
"Come now and let us reason together," etc.;
they shall be white as snow"
from the understanding of the heart.
that Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him, prayed
in order to enter the land
is always read on Shabbos Nachamu,
in order to strengthen the hearts
as it says in Midrash Tanchuma
since he has made a will,
he should no longer pray, etc.;
וְגַם הֲלֹא מִמֹּשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
and moreover from Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
שֶׁבְּחִינָה שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
the aspect of Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
is the aspect of the revelation
וְאִם הָיָה מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
had Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
the conduct there would have been
through the aspect of the Written Torah,
and the man would have come down to them
as it will be in the time to come:
וְאַתֶּם כֹּהֲנֵי ה׳ תִּקָּרֵאוּ וְגוֹ׳ (יְשַׁעְיָה סא, ה–ו)
"and you shall be called the kohanim of Hashem," etc. (Yeshayahu 61:5–6).
But the conduct of Eretz Yisrael
in the aspect of "Malchus is the mouth,
for Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him, to enter
And in order to fulfill the mitzvos
And as we have already said,
he reaches the intended purpose more,
than what he does in actuality,
according to the measure of the deed.
And therefore this parsha is read
in order to strengthen weak hands
in the seven weeks of consolation;
and so many Ends have passed,
And from this our heart will be steadfast,
even though we do not yet merit
let no man's heart fall within him;
all the prayers of the souls of Yisrael
according to the measure of its longing,
to be consoled in his heart;
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (תַּעֲנִית ל, ב)
as they said, of blessed memory (Taanis 30b):
the intent is not only to the time to come;
rather, according to the measure of the longing
in the inwardness of the heart,
and feel in his heart her joy,
in the aspect of "Rejoice in Hashem, O tzaddikim."
the whole text of the prayers was established
"Who causes the horn of salvation to sprout,"
let the children of Tziyon exult in their King."
